title: Identity provider
description: One identity provider a person may sign in with, under .ai/repo/identity/providers/. Every provider is reached through the same flow — the OpenID Connect authorization code flow with PKCE (S256) and a nonce, whose ID Token is verified against the provider's JSON Web Key Set, whose `iss` must equal `issuer`, and whose subject is read from `subject_claim` — so the shape below has no field that only one provider can fill and no place for a provider-specific extension. A provider is struck by deleting its file. The object names the environment variables its client id and client secret arrive in and never holds either value: no credential is written in this repository.

schema.description: The format version of this object. A version the tool does not know is refused, never guessed.

id.description: The identity of this provider within the repository, `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, equal to the file's name without `.yaml`. A display name is never an identity.

display_name.description: The name the sign-in offer shows a person, as the provider's own brand writes it.

description.description: One line: what this provider is, for a listing.

order.description: Where this provider stands in the sign-in offer: the offer lists providers by ascending order. Two providers of one repository do not share an order.

flow.description: The flow the provider is reached through. One value, because there is one flow: the OpenID Connect authorization code flow with PKCE (RFC 7636, S256) and a nonce. A provider that cannot be reached through it is not an identity provider of this kind; a second flow would be a new version of the schema, never a field of one object.

issuer.description: The OpenID Provider's issuer identifier (OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0, section 3): an https URL with no query and no fragment. An ID Token whose `iss` is not exactly this value is refused.

discovery.description: The provider's discovery document (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`), where the endpoints below can be checked against what the provider publishes. Optional and never a substitute for them: a discovery document need not carry every endpoint the code flow uses, so the endpoints are declared.

scopes.description: The scopes the authorization request asks for. `openid` is always among them, because without it the response carries no ID Token and no subject. Ask for no more than sign-in needs.

subject_claim.description: The ID Token claim that carries the stable identifier of the person at this provider. OpenID Connect Core names it `sub`; it is the only claim an account is bound to, never an e-mail address or a name, which a person can change.

url.description: An https URL. A query string is allowed, because some providers version an endpoint in its path and others do not; a fragment is not.

endpoints.description: The three endpoints the code flow reaches, each an https URL: where the person is sent to authenticate, where the code is exchanged for tokens, and where the keys that sign the ID Token are published.

authorization.description: The authorization endpoint (OpenID Connect Core 1.0, section 3.1.2).

token.description: The token endpoint (OpenID Connect Core 1.0, section 3.1.3). Reached from the server only, never from a browser.

jwks.description: The JSON Web Key Set the ID Token's signature is verified against (`jwks_uri`).

credentials.description: Where the client's credentials arrive: the names of two environment variables, never their values. A value written here — a client id, a client secret, a token — does not match the pattern and is refused.

client_id_env.description: The environment variable the client id arrives in.

client_secret_env.description: The environment variable the client secret arrives in. Read by the server at run time; never logged, never written to a file of this repository.

env.description: The name of an environment variable, `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*`: upper case, digits and underscores, and never a value.
